title: Why the decision value works
heading: Keep track of the halfway point.
description: At each next column, ask whether the ideal line is above or below the halfway point between the two candidate pixel centres. Because y grows down, reaching that midpoint means choosing the lower pixel. We choose the lower pixel when exactly tied.

explanation.title: Turn the midpoint test into integers
explanation.code:
D = 2 × dx × (ideal_y_next − (y + ½))
start: D = 2 × dy − dx
explanation.text: D is a scaled signed difference, not a distance in pixels. Negative means the ideal line has not reached the midpoint; zero or positive means it has. Moving one column adds 2 × dy. Moving down a row subtracts 2 × dx. After setup, only integer additions, subtractions and comparisons are needed.

explanation.title: The shallow, right-and-down case
explanation.code:
dx = x_end - x
dy = y_end - y
D = 2 * dy - dx
pixel(x, y)
while x < x_end:
    if D >= 0:
        y = y + 1
        D = D - 2 * dx
    x = x + 1
    D = D + 2 * dy
    pixel(x, y)
explanation.text: Read this algorithm: 0 ≤ dy ≤ dx and dx > 0. Steep lines exchange the roles of x and y; leftward or upward lines use negative steps. The next activity’s line(...) handles all directions for you. This reading example uses while; the small practice editor provides line(...) instead.
